posts.title: Pitch weeks for next season open on 1 December
posts.excerpt: Pitch weeks, Saturday to Saturday, for the coming season open for booking on 1 December.
posts.content:
Pitch weeks for next season open for booking on 1 December. A pitch week is seven nights, Saturday to Saturday, on a gravel touring pitch with 10A hook-up, and costs €210.

Call reception, write to hello@nohara-park.example or use the booking page. We hold the pitch for 48 hours, free of charge, and a 25% deposit confirms it. Hana Kovač answers within one working day.

posts.title: What the wardens do between November and March
posts.excerpt: A look inside the winter work of our seven-person team across eleven hectares of woodland, hedges, and pitches at Nohara Holiday Park.
posts.content:
When touring caravans depart on 2 November, a distinct change in rhythm settles over Nohara Holiday Park. The thirty-six gravel touring pitches and sixteen meadow grass pitches fall quiet, leaving eleven hectares of oak and ash trees under open autumn skies. For our team of seven wardens, however, November does not mark a pause. Instead, it begins four months of focused outdoor maintenance that keep the park orderly and ready for spring. While our fourteen timber lodges welcome visitors throughout winter, the grounds become the main focus of daily attention.

Winter work begins along Ash Hollow Lane throughout November and December. Here, warden Samir Haddad leads our traditional hedge laying. Using billhooks and wooden stakes, Samir cuts and lays mature hazel, hawthorn, and blackthorn branches along the boundary. This rural technique encourages dense fresh growth from the base in spring, creating a thick living barrier that shelters nesting birds and small wildlife from winter frost. By late December, the entire boundary hedge along the lane has been surveyed, staked, and neatly bound.

As January brings colder weather, work moves toward essential infrastructure. Head warden Tobias Weller and Samir inspect every drainage run across the park, clearing autumn leaf fall from culverts to ensure winter rains flow away from pitches toward the central pond. Inside our heated wash house, plumbing and hot water systems undergo complete servicing. Every pipe is checked and insulated, and shower fittings are descaled. Receptionist Hana Kovač and Tobias maintain regular office hours from 09:00 to 16:00 each day, answering enquiries for the coming year, with the office closing only on 25 and 26 December.

February is dedicated to forestry and woodland conservation. Founder Ingrid Halloran, who established the park in 2004 on a former tree nursery, continues to walk the 2.4-kilometre oak wood trail every morning at dawn. Working alongside Ingrid, Samir conducts our annual tree survey, examining the canopy of every mature oak and ash across the estate. Where branches have been weakened by winter winds, careful pruning keeps walking paths safe. Selected hazel coppice stools are cut back to ground level, admitting sunlight to the woodland floor where bluebells and wild garlic will emerge in April.

Throughout the winter period from November to mid-March, warden Luca Ferreira looks after our winter caravan storage yard. Up to thirty touring caravans are accommodated on dedicated hard standing, sheltered by mature trees. Luca conducts a thorough physical inspection of every caravan once a week, checking wheel clamps, corner steadies, and weatherproof covers. On dry winter mornings, Luca opens each caravan to ventilate the interior, preventing condensation and preserving fabrics. At €320 for the winter season, this service gives owners like Greta and Paul complete peace of mind until collection appointments begin in March.

Meanwhile, warden Amara Osei attends to our fourteen timber lodges. With ten two-bed lodges and four three-bed lodges open throughout winter, guests arrive weekly and on weekends to enjoy brisk forest walks and warm wood-burning stoves. Amara keeps every wood store stocked with dry split logs, checks flue seals, and ensures bed linen and towels are freshly laid out before every arrival. Down at the pond, warden Élodie Brun monitors water levels and clearing edges, preparing equipment for the Saturday pond mornings that return for visiting children when warmer weather arrives.

By early March, winter tasks turn toward reopening. Luca and Samir bring in fresh gravel to top up the thirty-six touring pitches, levelling tracks and checking that all 10A electric hook-up posts and water points within thirty metres are fully operational. Access roads are smoothed to maintain safe passage at our 8 km/h speed limit. When the timber gate opens on 15 March, Tobias will meet arriving families and walk them to their pitches, welcoming them to a park carefully tended through winter.

posts.title: Saturday pond mornings, from April
posts.excerpt: Nets, a white tray and a warden: pond mornings for children start in April.
posts.content:
From April, Élodie Brun takes children to the pond on Saturday mornings with nets and a white tray. They look at what lives in the water and put it back.

Pond mornings are free for guests. Ask at reception on Saturday morning; children under 5 should come with an adult.
